record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.original_question: For the implicit-memory models based on nonlocal perception and taxis, how do unequal parameter choices alter the broad pattern-formation insights already known from simplified settings? In particular, what roles are played by unequal diffusion rates, advection rates, perceptual radii, or different perceptual kernels, and do the previously observed qualitative trends survive under these asymmetries?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 56. How do different parameters change the broad insights obtained above? That is, what role might unequal diffusion rates, advection rates, perceptual radii, perceptual kernels etc. play in altering space use outcomes? Do the general trends highlighted above remain true? If not, under what conditions do these general trends change?

artifact.category_tag: nonlocal PDE models of animal movement
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-population implicit-memory model of animal movement on a bounded spatial domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (with no-flux boundary conditions), in which each population $u_i(x,t)$, $i=1,2$, evolves by diffusion and by an advective taxis driven by nonlocal perception of the other population. A representative system is
\[
\partial_t u_i = D_i\,\Delta u_i - \nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl(\alpha_i\, u_i\, \nabla (K_i * u_j)\bigr), \qquad i\neq j\in\{1,2\},
\]
where $D_i>0$ are diffusion coefficients, $\alpha_i\in\mathbb{R}$ are advection (taxis) coefficients, and $K_i$ are radially symmetric, nonnegative perceptual kernels of perceptual radius $R_i>0$ (e.g. top-hat $K_i(x)=\mathbf{1}_{|x|\le R_i}/|B_{R_i}|$, Gaussian, or exponential), with $K_i*u_j(x)=\int_\Omega K_i(x-y)u_j(y)\,dy$ (suitably extended).

In the symmetric case $D_1=D_2$, $\alpha_1=\alpha_2$, $R_1=R_2$, $K_1=K_2$, linear stability analysis and numerical simulation reveal qualitative pattern-formation phenomena (e.g. thresholds for Turing-type instability, segregation versus aggregation of the two populations, formation of stationary or oscillatory patterns).

Problem. Analyze rigorously, by linear stability, weakly nonlinear, and global bifurcation analysis, how the introduction of asymmetries
(i) unequal diffusion rates $D_1\neq D_2$,
(ii) unequal advection/taxis rates $\alpha_1\neq \alpha_2$,
(iii) unequal perceptual radii $R_1\neq R_2$,
(iv) different perceptual kernel shapes $K_1\neq K_2$,
alters the symmetric-case conclusions. Specifically:
  (a) Determine the modified instability thresholds and dispersion relations as functions of the asymmetry parameters.
  (b) Identify which qualitative trends (existence and type of nontrivial steady states, segregation/aggregation behavior, bifurcation structure, and long-time space-use patterns) persist under each asymmetry, and characterize the precise parameter regimes in which they fail.
  (c) Provide explicit conditions on $(D_i,\alpha_i,R_i,K_i)$ delineating regime changes in the pattern-formation outcomes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2022 survey on PDE models for animal movement with nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping. No web search result indicates a complete resolution; subsequent work has examined particular asymmetric cases of nonlocal advection-diffusion systems but a full classification of the effect of unequal diffusion/advection rates, perceptual radii, and kernel shapes on the symmetric-case pattern-formation conclusions does not appear to be established.
